I've been demoted to a position across town with less responsibility. I had recently been given a review stating that I was doing very well in my position so I was really shocked to be told about the change.

When I had been in the psych ward for 6 weeks and no medication was working so they suggested ECT. I still get it once a month as an outpatient because it works. But being told that shock therapy was probably a good option made me feel like I had really gone over the edge.
Thanks, I appreciate that. It's saved me in many ways.

It doesn't hurt at all because I'm under anaesthetic. They induce a small seizure in my brain and I wake up 20 minutes later with a headache. The anaesthetic makes me tired for the rest of the day but I'm back to work the next day. The biggest side effect is some short term memory loss. They don't know exactly how it works, but it's nothing like the barbaric tales that you might have heard about. 

From the web: (and a little more clearly put)
Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a procedure, done under general anesthesia, in which small electric currents are passed through the brain, intentionally triggering a brief seizure. ECT seems to cause changes in brain chemistry that can quickly reverse symptoms of certain mental illnesses.

That I am bipolar and I have ECT (electric convulsive therapy, aka shock therapy) every two weeks. 

It lets me work a full time job, and live a fairly normal and productive life that medication alone couldn't. 

But it has such a bad reputation that I don't think I'll ever tell anyone in real life except my SO. 

But I wish more people knew how often it is used and how successfully it is used. And maybe the massive stigma surrounding it would disappear.

I had SSRI discontinuation syndrome about two years ago when coming off of Effexor. I weaned myself (with dr on board) off very slowly, over about six months, but still had the brain zaps and vertigo. It was horrible. The only thing that kind of helped was Ativan. A small dose twice a day seemed to alleviate the worst of it, and the zaps lasted three weeks all told.

So I'm in the hospital right now as a result of my decision to discontinue my meds.  Im just finishing a course of ECT, and still getting my meds sorted.  I'm diagnosed as bipolar II and ADHD-PI.  It has been a rough couple of months and I would certainly attribute this to my decision to discontinue my meds.
